OSTQuant employs a learnable equivalent transformation, consisting of an orthogonal transformation and a scaling transformation, to optimize the distributions of weights and activations across the entire quantization space.
All activations are quantized using pertoken asymmetric quantization without any pruning operations, while weights are quantized using symmetric per-channel quantization.

ev.section: A.4 INFERENCE EFFICIENCY AND QUANTIZATION OVERHEAD
ev.quote: The inference environment features an Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 5317 CPU and an Nvidia 3090 GPU.

strengths.value: Provides a principled metric (QSUR) with mathematical derivations linking transformation choice to quantization accuracy.

ev.quote: We introduce the concept of Quantization Space Utilization Rate (QSUR) as an effective metric to evaluate quantizability. We also complement QSUR with mathematical derivations that examine the effects and limitations of various transformations

strengths.value: Sets state-of-the-art W4A4KV4 results, beating SpinQuant by about 1 zero-shot point on multiple LLaMA models.

ev.quote: Even in the highly challenging 4-4-4 setting, our approach retains a significant performance gain, outperforming the SOTA method, SpinQuant, by around 1 point across multiple models.

strengths.value: Fast calibration: quantizes LLaMA-3-8B in roughly 20 minutes on a single A800 GPU using 150 iterations.

ev.quote: it can complete the quantization of LLaMA-3-8B on an A800 GPU in just 20 minutes.

strengths.value: Transformations fuse into existing weights, so deployment has zero extra parameters or runtime overhead.

ev.quote: After optimization, O and Λ can be directly merged into the existing weights, meaning no additional computational overhead or parameters are introduced during deployment, ensuring efficient inference.

weaknesses.value: Cross-entropy loss alone overfits the small calibration set, requiring the new KL-Top heuristic to recover zero-shot scores.

ev.quote: directly applying original cross-entropy (CE) loss can result in accuracy drop. As shown in Tab 1, despite the quantized model exhibiting lower perplexity ... its performance on zero-shot tasks declines.

weaknesses.value: KL-Top wins zero-shot but increases Wiki PPL versus the origin loss (e.g. LLaMA-2-7B 5.94 vs 5.38).
Below 4-bit weight-only quantization still incurs a sharp accuracy drop, limiting use of very low bit widths.

ev.section: A.4 INFERENCE EFFICIENCY AND QUANTIZATION OVERHEAD
ev.quote: quantizing the weights to below 4 bits leads to a significant drop in accuracy.

weaknesses.value: Full activation quantization for ROPE and SiLU is left as future work, so current results stop at W4A4KV4.

limitations.value: Hardware tests are limited to data-center GPUs (3090, A800, A6000); no edge or mobile NPU evaluation is provided.
